front: How long is 1° of latitude, and how does 1° of longitude vary?
back: About 111 km. 1° of longitude is about 111.3 × cos(latitude) km, shrinking to zero at the poles.
Decimal $=$ degrees $+$ minutes $\div 60$ $+$ seconds $\div 3600$; south and west are negative.
Local time changes by 4 minutes per degree of longitude (360° in 24 h); places east are ahead.
60 zones, each 6° wide, numbered from 180°; Zimbabwe lies in zones 35S and 36S.

front: Three projection families and what they suit?
back: Cylindrical (Mercator): navigation, shape. Conical: mid-latitude countries. Azimuthal: polar regions and direction from a centre.
Forward: latitude and longitude to x and y. Inverse: x and y back to latitude and longitude.
Shape (conformal), area (equal-area), distance (equidistant) and direction (azimuthal); never all four.
The same coordinates mean different ground positions in different datums; mixing datums misaligns layers.
